6.name: Marcus agrees to reduced rate

6.name: Asha accepts Marcus's offer

evidence: Bridgepoint needed a signed transfer packet, a physician's order, and a deposit wired before Friday at five, and the admissions coordinator there had already left one message about a bed that would not hold past the weekend.

evidence: With her thumb she thumbed out a message to Marcus on the phone in her lap—I'll handle everything, just send me your email—and watched the screen until the delivered tag appeared, because she did not yet trust that he would still be reachable in an hour.

6.name: Asha summons nursing supervisor

6.name: Asha demands discharge paperwork

6.name: supervisor agrees to page doctor

Before the read receipt came up

6.name: asha ignores marcus reply

evidence: Asha read it twice and did not answer, because answering would mean explaining to Marcus that Daniel had no standing here and risking Marcus hearing only the old shape of the argument and going quiet again.

6.name: holds father's hand and waits

she gave her name, her father's room number, and asked plainly whether the attending had acknowledged the page about the Bridgepoint transfer

Asha thanked her by name and asked for the clerk's name in return, so that when she called again there would be a person on the other end who had already said yes

evidence: She opened the third one first and read the line she needed, then read it again because she had expected a different name, and the small administrative fact rearranged what she thought the next call was going to sound like.

6.name: enters Lucia as proxy

evidence: Asha typed Lucia's name into the proxy field on the Bridgepoint portal—Lucia, not Daniel, not Marcus, the sister whose hands had stayed under their father's elbows for a decade while the rest of them sent checks or didn't—and hit submit before she could let the surprise of it slow her down.

evidence: The confirmation banner loaded green at the top of the page

6.name: calls Trenton supervisor

because the supervisor had picked up and she needed her voice steady

Asha laid out the three facts in the order she needed them heard: Lucia held the proxy, the discharge order was expected within the hour, and her father would be transferred to Bridgepoint before the Friday cutoff, not held over for a state bed.

6.name: Supervisor concedes the argument

evidence: The supervisor made the small acknowledging sounds people make when they have already lost an argument they had not yet started

6.name: Asha ends call without softening
6.description: Asha thanks the supervisor and hangs up quickly before the conversation can become gentler.
evidence: Asha thanked her and ended the call before any softening could happen.

6.name: Asha calls Lucia about proxy

evidence: Then she dialed Lucia, watching her father's chest rise under the thin blanket
and when Lucia picked up Asha said her name first and the word proxy second, and waited.

6.name: Lucia agrees to be ready quickly

evidence: She told Lucia a ride was coming and to bring her ID, and did not yet say whose car it would be.

evidence: Asha picked the phone back up and called Rosa, and when Rosa answered on the first ring Asha said only that Lucia needed to be at a notary in the next ninety minutes and that Daniel was not driving her.

evidence: Whatever Daniel said back, he gave her the address; Rosa texted Asha a single line a moment later, on the way, which was all Asha needed to know that the signature would be where it had to be before the cutoff.

6.name: Asha calls Marcus for the deposit

She gave him the routing numbers slowly, the way she would read them to a client

the wire was real.

evidence: She gave him the routing numbers slowly, the way she would read them to a client, and then stopped talking, because she had learned in the last hour that her silence did more work than her sentences.

When the line picked up she said the wire had cleared, that she expected the attending's discharge order and the medication reconciliation in her inbox within the hour, and named Bridgepoint by full address so it could not later be transcribed as somewhere else.
